- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

## Contract review

- **(a) The four skill files — retired text goes, kept text stays, with one exception below.** `SKILL.md` 819 → 815: the label-hang bullets (:342, :656–:658), the `--pair` / parking / double-carrier bullets, the gate-label clause of the label-write rule (:154–:155), the SELF-REVIEW readout (:239) and the 「不得自审自合 … 复核由另一座位」 half of :25 go — the red line 「⛔ 永不合自己的 PR」 at :27 stays, so nothing a seat may not do is lost; :653 keeps 「PASS ⇒ ready、auto-merge;FAIL ⇒ 补丁轮;⛔ 免复核不放行」. `references/contract-review.md` 60 → 24: the 〈载体纪律〉 and 〈降档保险丝〉 sections are deleted whole as ruled, the pure-regeneration exception line (#19244) survives under pre-check ①, the record's shape (`Served-tier:` = the constant name, `Head-sha:`, `Implemented-by:` / `Reviewed-by:` as record lines) and who renders it stay, the landing pre-check reads two items (record PASS; checks green). `core-rules.md` 151 → 151: the two mirrored clauses trimmed in step with SKILL.md. `platform-readings.md` 469 → 467: the `--pair` proxy reading and two fuse clauses go; the served-tier readings stay.
- **(b) One line went that the maintainer's word of this date keeps — the owed change.** `platform-readings.md:394` 「强制档不得因不可用而降档 —— 那正是降档保险丝要拒的替换。」 was deleted as a fuse rule. Its first half IS the principle the maintainer stated today (「某个agent临时没有fable给的特殊授权,不应该改变skills」) and the reversal card #19680 was filed on; with the fuse section gone, that line was the skills text's only statement of it (the dispatch-gates.mjs docblock is code). It must come back as a standalone rule without the fuse name — e.g. 「强制档不得因一次会话拿不到而降档:临缺授权 ≠ 退役,退役恒维护者裁决;不达档改走隔离达档子代理或等档。」 (≤ 120 bytes; the file has headroom 467 / 469). Nothing else in the four files is owed.
- **(c) The declaration semantics — a note, not owed.** The deleted 〈载体纪律〉 section also carried the `Clause-②` declaration guidance (the mechanical floor: a new exported symbol or a new key on a published payload is always `yes`; conformance is not mechanised; when unsure declare `yes`). The ruling retires the section by name and KEEPS the declaration line and its reader; the criterion survives in `SKILL.md` :649–:651, `AGENTS.md:1084` and `dispatch-gates.mjs --tier`'s clause-② line. Recorded so nobody reads the deletion as retiring the declaration.
- **(d) `scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs` — right, and the harness story is honest.** The two self-test cases asserting the deleted fuse sentences are replaced by ONE retirement guard in the file's own retired-spelling pattern: 「the rulebook no longer carries the retired 降档保险丝 lines」, negating both regexes, reds if the text creeps back; the `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` spelling case stays. The plain removal was refused by the harness twice (「Security Test Removal」) and was not routed around; the guard form (a different, honest change asserting the new truth) was accepted. Measured by this seat: 1905 cases in the detached self-test at this head (the dev's reading; the seat's own detached run is read before any landing act), and the prose-only head `6900454` read 2 of 1904 red — the expected direction. The docblock beside `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` still points at 「references/contract-review.md 「降档保险丝」」 — a dangling section name, step ③'s rider.
- **(e) `error-code-ledger.zod.ts:102` and its generated page — right, and the changeset is the second owed change.** The docblock sentence no longer names the label; the Clause-② statement stays; `content/docs/references/api/error-code-ledger.mdx` is regenerated (the diff is exactly the sentence; `check:generated` 「all 15 artifacts up to date」). The dev MEASURED the dispatch's 「no emitted dist byte」 assumption false: the file-level docblock is emitted into two `.d.ts` chunks (12 of 216 dist files differ, runtime JS identical), and `@objectstack/spec` `files[]` ships `src/**/*.zod.ts` — so this diff publishes bytes from a released package. `AGENTS.md:1083` — 「⛔ never `skip-changeset`: that label is for a diff that publishes nothing from any released package」 — is the stricter clause against os-dev.md's 「注释不发布」 fast lane, whose premise this measurement falsifies for file-level docblocks; by the skill's own conflict rule the stricter one wins: a `patch` changeset for `@objectstack/spec` (a documentation line: the ledger docblock no longer names a retired PM label) is owed, and the seat removes `skip-changeset` at the landing act.
- **(f) Nothing narrowed or widened.** The ruling's file list is honoured; the two declared increments (the generated page; the two self-test cases) are required by the diff, not elective. `AGENTS.md:278` (Prime Directive #14 naming `--pair` and the label) is Tier H, step ③, untouched; six other references still name the retired machinery (`os-dev.md:303`, `dispatch-runbook.md:161`, `lanes/director.md:27` / `:35`, `lanes/ui.md:38`, `state-machine.md:10`) plus `SKILL.md:769` — step ③'s riders, correctly not widened here.
- **(g) Gates — re-run by this seat on its own worktree at this head.** `check:pm-skill-ratchet` (815 / 819, 24 / 60, 151 / 151, 467 / 469 — all under, ceilings untouched), `check:pm-skill-id-lint`, `check:skill-frame-sync`, `check:pm-governed-prose`, `check:doc-authoring`, `check:nul-bytes`, `check-skills-token-ratchet`, `check-skill-frame-freshness`, `check:pm-clause2-carriers` (1140), the queue guard's self-test (312), `check:pm-half-states` (5160) — all exit 0; `check-governed-merges.mjs --pr 19694` exit 3 — GOVERNED, four `.claude/**` paths, 96 lines. The dev's 127-family derivation and `--ran` (124 run, 3 NOT-MEASURED — whole-repo build prerequisites, CI's) read as reported.

### ② Semver level

The `skip-changeset` label on the PR is the wrong carrier by `AGENTS.md:1083` and comes off when the changeset lands.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Tier — a register reading against the ruling's word.** `check-governed-merges.mjs --pr 19694` reads Tier S (`.claude/**` whole); ruling 5770886272 wrote 「Execution order (Tier H — `.claude/**` and `AGENTS.md`; the maintainer merges)」. The ruling's word is the stricter and names the merger: this PR stays draft for the maintainer's hand; the seat's record and ACCEPT are the review, not the landing. Reported for the maintainer to keep or lift.
- **The harness refusals** (verbatim reasons in the report) are recorded, not worked around; the saved plain-removal patch is superseded by the accepted guard and is not applied.
- **The PR body carries a stale §C expected-red list** written before the guard landed — the seat PATCHes the body with the dev's replacement at ACCEPT, after the patch head.
- **`git fetch --unshallow`** in the shared object store (history only) so one self-test could reach a verdict — declared, harmless.
- **CI at this head**: `Lint & Repo Gates` in_progress at the seat's read, the rest green.

**Must change before this record can read PASS:** (1) restore the principle line in `references/platform-readings.md` as a standalone rule without the fuse name (①(b)); (2) add a `patch` changeset for `@objectstack/spec` describing the docblock change (①(e), ②). Both small and local; nothing in the retirement itself needs rework.
